sources.locator: "War in Donbas", revision 1370749630, lead and § Protests in the Donbas

explanation: The article runs the one into the other. Its § Protests in the Donbas opens “Following the revolution, counter-revolutionary and pro-Russian protests began in parts of the Donbas” and, of 6 April, “demonstrators in Donetsk demanded a referendum on autonomy or accession to Russia”; six days later “unmarked pro-Russian militants seized the Donetsk headquarters of the Interior Ministry and two police stations without resistance”, which is where this record begins. `enabled`: the protests are the ground the armed seizures were made on and not an order to make them, and the lead gives the war’s own movers as “Russian-backed paramilitaries”.
